transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Please have a seat. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I came in because most days I just feel like I’m stuck at the bottom of some dark hole. It’s hard to explain. I’ll be around people I know, like at work or even just out somewhere, and it’s like I’m still completely alone in it.

I kept thinking I could just push through it—my dad always used to say you don’t complain, you just get the job done, especially in hands-on work—but this heavy, hopeless feeling just doesn’t lift. It’s there most of the time.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things anymore—like activities you used to like or even time with friends and family?

Yeah… that’s been one of the worst parts, I think. I used to really love hiking, and painting, and going down to the makerspace to tinker with stuff. Even at work, if there was a tricky install, I used to get kind of absorbed in figuring it out.

Now I’ll have the paint supplies sitting right there, or tools laid out, and I just… stare at them. Or I ignore calls from people because the thought of going out or even talking just feels like too much, like none of it is worth starting. It’s strange, because I used to be the kind of person who always had some project going. My garage is full of half-finished things now.
How long have you been feeling this way? When did you first start noticing these feelings?

It’s been… about a year and a couple months now, I think. It really started after last fall, when I had that fall on the HVAC job and hurt my back. Things kind of started unraveling from there.

I remember because it was around the time the weather was changing, and I was still trying to act like I could just keep working the way I always did. I kept telling myself it was temporary, you know, like when a part’s on backorder and you just work around it for a while. But it didn’t pass. It’s been there since then.
Have you noticed any periods of time during this last year when your mood improved significantly for a few days or more, even briefly, before going back to how you’ve been feeling?

I don’t know… not really that I can point to. I mean, there might be a day where the sun’s out or I get some little thing done and I think, okay, maybe I’m not completely useless today, but it doesn’t feel like a real shift for a few days or anything.

It’s funny, I used to measure weeks by jobs—like, “oh, that was the week with the busted rooftop unit,” or “that was the week I repainted the kitchen cabinets”—but lately it all kind of blurs together. So… I guess no, I haven’t noticed any real stretch where it lifted much.

Have you ever experienced a period of time when your mood was unusually elevated, irritable, or you felt like you had much more energy than usual—maybe even to the point where you didn’t need much sleep or felt like you could take on a lot of tasks at once?

Um… I don’t think so. Not like that, anyway.

I mean, I’ve had times where I get wound up, especially if something at work used to go wrong and everyone’s standing around waiting on me, and I’d sort of kick into gear—but that’s not really a “good mood” thing. That’s more like… pressure, you know? Like when a unit won’t start and you’ve got three people asking if it’s fixed yet.

But no, I can’t really think of a stretch where I was suddenly full of energy or didn’t need sleep and was taking on everything. If anything, lately it feels more like the opposite… but I’m not sure if I’m answering what you mean.
Have there been specific times over the past year when you felt your low mood was particularly bad, or has it been more of a steady, ongoing feeling without clear peaks and valleys?

It’s mostly steady, I think… like it doesn’t really let up. I came in because most days I feel like I’m just sitting at the bottom of this dark hole, and even if I’m around people I know, it’s still there.

I mean, sometimes I’ll be at the hardware store or talking to somebody I’ve known forever, and I’m nodding along, but inside it’s just this heavy, hopeless feeling. Like I can’t quite climb out of it. There might be moments where I’m distracted, but I wouldn’t say there are clear ups and downs so much as… it’s just been hanging over everything.
Over the past year, have you had any periods—even just a few days long—when your mood improved enough that you felt like your old self, even if it didn’t last?

Not really, no. I keep trying to think if there was a few days where I felt like “me” again, but… I don’t think so.

I mean, I’ll have little moments, like if I run into someone I know and we talk about something normal—like their water heater going out or some dumb thing at the hardware store—and for a minute I’m just answering like I would’ve before. But underneath it, it’s still there. I came in because most days it feels like I’m sitting at the bottom of a dark hole, and even around people I know I can’t shake that heavy, hopeless feeling.

So… no, I wouldn’t say I’ve had a stretch where it really lifted.
Before this past year, have you ever had a period of time where you felt persistently down, hopeless, or lost interest in things for several weeks or more?

I’m not sure… I mean, I’ve had rough patches before, like anybody, I guess. There were times when work was stressful or money was tight, and I’d get worn down.

Like, when I was doing installs full-time, there’d be weeks where everything went wrong—wrong parts ordered, customers upset, crawling around in some basement with bad lighting—and I’d come home just kind of beat. But I don’t know if that’s the same as what you’re asking.

Before this past year… I can’t really say I remember a stretch where I was down like this for weeks and weeks. Not that stands out clearly. This feels different, or maybe I’m just noticing it more now. I don’t know.
Have you ever had a period in your life before this past year when you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things for more than two weeks at a time?

Before this past year? I don’t know… I keep trying to sort it out, but it all kind of blurs together.

I’ve had bad times, sure, but this is the thing that made me come in—most days now it feels like I’m down at the bottom of some dark hole. Even if I’m around people I know, like somebody from town or a customer I’ve seen a hundred times, I can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling.

So if you mean like this, for more than two weeks… I don’t remember it being this way before. Not like this.
Have you had any period of at least two months when you were not experiencing these low mood symptoms at all, between when you were younger and this past year?

Two months? I… I don’t really know how to measure it going back like that. I mean, when I was younger there were normal stretches, I guess—work, errands, fixing things, talking to people at the hardware store or wherever—but this past year is what’s been different.

Now it’s most days, like I’m sitting at the bottom of a dark hole. Even if I’m around people I know, I can’t shake that heavy, hopeless feeling. So… if you mean recently, no, I haven’t had a couple months where it was just gone. Going way back before this year, I’m not sure.
